correctness.rationale: For Boolean cube Q_d d>=3 with unit edges, d-edge connectivity ensures every two-link deletion remains connected, and K(G)=N tr(L^+). Walsh diagonalization gives L^+ and (L^+)^2 distance kernels g_{1,d}(k),g_{2,d}(k). The heat-kernel integral proves positive strictly decreasing a_k and b_k; mixed edge incidence x,y are either (2a_k,2b_k) for parallel edges separated by k>=1 or (a_k-a_{k+1},b_k-b_{k+1}) for distinct coordinate directions separated by k>=0. Rank-two Woodbury yields increase 2N(hS+xy)/(h^2-x^2), strictly increasing in x,y. Therefore compare only closest parallel and adjacent perpendicular. Tilting positive measures by 1+q shows a0/a1 and b0/b1 strictly grow in dimension; at d>=8 both exceed 3, and at d3..7 exact rational gaps are strictly positive. Equality iff perpendicular edges share one vertex; optimizer count N*binom(d,2). Independent exact rational spectral enumeration checked all orbit classes d3..9, reproducing d3 172/15,d4 502/51,d5 2696/245 and strict gaps. Finite checks do not substitute for the all-d integral comparison.
residual_risks: Graph is unit-conductance unweighted simple Q_d and exactly two existing edges deleted; no weights, k>2 or d=2 considered
The dimension-eight threshold uses exact b0-3b1=1007/1204224; independent spectral samples support but do not prove increasing-ratio lemma

originality.rationale: Electrical effective-resistance loss differs from shortest-path distance leverage. The complete hypercube Kirchhoff index from Liu et al and general resistance matrices are existing tools; Tamura (2026) applies deleted-edge defect matrices to complete graphs K_n-F, not to cube Q_d with nonconstant Green kernel. The submitted result gives the new strict extremizer geometry for deleting exactly two edges of any-dimensional cube. The 1992 paper “On a leverage problem in the hypercube” shares the graph and edge-failure language, but its accessible abstract concerns shortest-path leverage. Full text could not be accessed even via authorized Oxford, so do not assert exhaustive noncoverage.
residual_risks: Hamburger/Pippert/Weakley 1992 original full text unavailable; accessible abstract distinguishes shortest-path leverage, but potential stronger unpublished calculations are not excluded.
Tamura 2026 defect method may admit extensions to vertex-transitive graphs; only complete-graph statement was accessible, so generic method overlap must be acknowledged.
General graph edge-failure Kirchhoff optimization literature may have a dominating theorem not indexed by the specific cube name.

value.rationale: The strict worst-case pair of two failed links in every-dimensional canonical hypercube network is a natural topology-and-resilience extremal question. The answer is counterintuitively local (incident edges) and has an exact rational magnitude and equality orbit, requiring nontrivial Green-kernel and all-d monotonicity work. The classification is meaningful without a general arbitrary-graph theorem.
residual_risks: Only two edge removals and unit conductances; random/multi-link failures are not covered
An implicit known edge-centrality theorem might reduce priority.
